newsitem.title: INDIA: India telephone support operations affected.
newsitem.headline: India telephone support operations affected.

text.p: India's telephone network was functioning normally on Wednesday despite a strike but some support services were hit by the indefinite work stoppage, a senior telephone company official said on Wednesday.

The official of the Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) told Reuters that all telephone exchanges in India were automatic, and telephone calls would not be affected as long as there was no need for help from employees.
Around one million telecommunication and postal workers launched an indefinite strike on Wednesday demanding higher annual bonus payments.
"Things are normal to the extent that automatic exchanges are not affected," the official told Reuters by telephone.
But trunk calls, office operations and phone enquiry services were disrupted by the strike, he said, adding that work was hit where ground staff, linesmen or clerks were needed.
"If a telephone is working it is perfect. But if it is faulty, there is no one to repair it," the official said.
